mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved in each of the last four weekly means (from -52.7 to -30.7), and this monotone convergence toward baseline carries its own momentum: returning footfall begets further footfall, so the next 28-day mean sits above the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose every week across t-3w to t-0w: -52.7, -42.7, -34.4, -30.7
failure_condition: The 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC after the decision point is at or below -40.1, the mean of the last four weekly prints, meaning the weekly series stalled or reversed.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week jump in PARKS larger than 10 points (from -19.4 to -6.9) marks outdoor-activity normalization; the household mobility budget expands beyond the home, and the extra out-of-home trips lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 10 points week-on-week (observed: -19.4 at t-1w to -6.9 at t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gained 12.5 points between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: In the two weeks following any PARKS week-on-week gain above 10 points, RETAIL_REC is flat or lower.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recovery are jointly necessary for retail recovery: returning commuters pass through transit corridors and generate adjacent retail trips. Only when both series improve in the same week does RETAIL_REC's four-week mean rise.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by at least 2 points and WORKPLACES improves by at least 1 point in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved -54.9 to -41.7 and WORKPLACES improved -30.7 to -23.9 over the four weeks
failure_condition: Weeks in which TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve are not followed by an increase in the RETAIL_REC 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL excess is decaying (14.4 to 9.4) but stays positive, so households still spend more time at home than baseline; each point of decay releases discretionary trips that land disproportionately in retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 10 while remaining above 0
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically from 14.4 at t-3w to 9.4 at t-0w while staying positive
regime_hint: gradual reopening with residual stay-at-home excess
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is flat or lower in the two weeks following any further weekly decline in RESIDENTIAL.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS normalization outpaces retail recovery (-37.3 to -6.9 versus -52.7 to -30.7), so discretionary out-of-home time is absorbed by outdoor recreation; this substitution diverts trips away from retail venues and stalls RETAIL_REC, pushing the next 28-day mean below the last.
candidate_trigger: PARKS moves at least 10 points closer to baseline than RETAIL_REC within a single week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gained 30.4 points over four weeks while RETAIL_REC gained 22.0, widening the parks-retail gap
failure_condition: The 28-day RETAIL_REC mean after the decision point exceeds -40.1 even while the PARKS-minus-RETAIL_REC gap continues to widen.

mechanism_narrative: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM (-9.9) and RETAIL_REC (-30.7) is narrowing from the essential side; as grocery and pharmacy trips stop substituting for discretionary shopping, retail traffic reabsorbs that flow and RETAIL_REC rises within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:the GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC gap narrowed from 31.6 points at t-3w to 20.8 points at t-0w
failure_condition: The next weekly RETAIL_REC print fails to rise in any week in which the GROCERY_PHARM minus RETAIL_REC gap narrows further.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal spring greening drives the PARKS surge (-37.3 to -6.9); the same weather shift raises unplanned retail-and-recreation trips such as walk-in errands and outdoor dining, so RETAIL_REC rises in the week after PARKS turns up.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 5 points over a two-week window
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 32.5 points between t-2w and t-0w, a two-week gain far above 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the week following a two-week PARKS gain above 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains the deepest-depressed category (-41.7) under partial restriction easing; once TRANSIT crosses above -40 the binding constraint on non-essential travel is effectively lifted, and retail footfall accelerates, raising the four-week RETAIL_REC mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT crosses above -40% for the first time
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has improved every week (-54.9 to -41.7) and is within 1.7 points of the -40 threshold at t-0w
regime_hint: restriction easing with transit capacity still constrained
failure_condition: After TRANSIT rises above -40, the following 28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the preceding 28-day mean.
